security_spec.violation_condition: In the Linux kernel, when the RISC-V vector context (vtype CSR) is saved/restored during context switch, signal delivery, or ptrace access, if the kernel's save/restore mask for vtype does not cover bits [XLEN-7:XLEN-2] (lambda[2:0], altfmt_A, altfmt_B, bs), then one process's IME tile geometry, input format, signedness, block-size configuration silently leaks to or is corrupted for another process. Similarly, if the kernel writes an unsupported lambda encoding (0b000 or >max WARL) on restore but the CPU silently drops it, the process resumes with wrong K_eff and register-layout semantics, causing silent data corruption. For KVM, failure to switch these vtype bits across VM entries/exits leaks guest IME configuration between VMs or between VM and host.
security_spec.summary: Zvvm adds lambda[2:0]/altfmt_A/altfmt_B/bs fields to vtype CSR at high bits; kernel context-switch/signal/ptrace/KVM paths must save/restore these bits or leak IME config across process boundaries
